newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi to meet metal unions, bosses on Fri.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to meet metal unions, bosses on Fri.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi called for a meeting of unions and management on Friday to discuss the long-running dispute in the metalworker and engineering sector, the prime minister's office said.
The leaders of Italy's big three trades union federations on Monday asked for Prodi to intervene in the pay dispute which has been dragging on since June.
A spokesman for Prodi said the prime minister would probably meet the metalworker unions and the federation of metalworker employers, Federmeccanica, on Friday morning.
The government has already intervened once in the dispute, suggesting in December that management give workers an average 200,000 lire per month pay increase.
Unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire increase, accepted the proposals but Federmeccanica has stuck to its original 139,000 lire offer.

Employers' groups say the government plan is inflationary. They are seeking a lower pay deal for workers in underdeveloped southern Italy and also want tax breaks to lessen the impact of any eventual accord.
The dispute, which involves some 1.7 million workers, is expected to set the tone for pay deals in a number of other Italian industrial sectors.

Metalworker unions have already staged three one-day stoppages to press their claims and leaders of Italy's main three union federations have threatened to call a general strike if management do not accept the government proposal. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
